workTitle: Symphony No. 6 in B minor, Op. 74

clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: Last symphony, B minor. It does not end with a bang — the finale is a long, sinking Adagio that just fades. He conducted the premiere himself. Nine days later he was dead.

clues.label: Places the composer lived and worked
clues.text: Born in a factory town in a huge empire to the east. Split his working life between two capitals — one old, one built on a northern river — and wrote this last symphony at a quiet house outside the newer one.

clues.label: A relationship with a contemporary
clues.text: A wealthy widow paid his bills for years. They wrote hundreds of letters and made a rule: they would never meet. When the money and the letters stopped, it wrecked him.

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: He taught at a new conservatory in the newer capital, toured as a celebrity conductor, and had one disastrous brief marriage. Critics at home often called the music too western. Audiences everywhere else could not get enough.

clues.label: An anecdote
clues.text: Swan Lake. The Christmas ballet with the Sugar Plum Fairy. The 1812 Overture — the one with actual cannons. The piano concerto that opens with those huge chords. You have heard him. Everyone has heard him.

explanation.summary: The sinking last movement, the widow who never met him, and Swan Lake: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, writing the Sixth Symphony in Russia in 1893.

points.text: A symphony that dies away in a slow finale, premiered by the composer, who was dead within days — that's the Pathétique, October 1893.
The empire is Russia. The capitals are Moscow and St Petersburg. He wrote this one at his house in Klin.
The widow is Nadezhda von Meck. Fourteen years of letters, zero meetings, then a sudden break in 1890.
He taught at the Moscow Conservatory. The short marriage to Antonina Miliukova lasted weeks and went badly.
Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, the 1812 Overture, Piano Concerto No. 1. If you have been in a room with a speaker, you have heard Tchaikovsky.
